messages:
sara: quick follow-up to the pinning schema RFC. idea: a 'subsumption cohort' concept where the control plane can temporarily treat small, provenance-preserving variant updates as a single logical pin for routing/telemetry while still preserving per-inference auditability.

mike: interesting. biggest worry = hidden regressions. how do you prove two variants are safe to subsume? we need deterministic criteria and an owner-signed attestation.

yun: agree. onboarding must emit an attestation (attest_id) and delta metrics vs a canonical validation harness. platform runs a lightweight verification and emits a cohort_score. cohort allowed only if score >= threshold and owner opted-in.

kevin: minimal rollout metadata fields (proposal):

```
subsum_cohort_id: optional string
cohort_ttl_days: optional int
cohort_policy: enum("strict","permissive")
attestation_id: optional string
cohort_score: optional float
cohort_pools: optional list
deprecation_phase: enum("soft","notice","hard")
deprecation_eta: optional string (timestamp)
```

sara: router behavior: if cohort exists, routing may map requests to any member variant unless tenant pin present. tenant pin wins. also mark telemetry with `subsum_cohort_id` and record exact `variant_hash` in audit logs.

lucas: implementation note: compute subsum_cohort_id deterministically (sha256(sorted variant hashes + owner_id + attestation_id)) so replicas/backfills converge. store canonical member list and formed_ts.

anna: ops flag: autoscaler needs to know pool affinity. require `cohort_pools` to list compatible pools. if members span incompatible pools, routing must respect pool_fallback_policy: enum("prefer","mirror","reject").

ops-bot: infra-bot: Canary started for variant v7-quant on canary/2026-06-02 :rocket:

mike: deprecation lifecycle: soft = group + telemetry; notice = notify tenants + suggested migration; hard = reject/redirect. include `deprecation_phase` and `deprecation_eta` so UI can display clear timelines.

yun: add tenant opt-out: tenant_meta.allow_subsumption: bool. default true for public tenants, false for regulated customers. opt-out should be applied immediately to avoid surprise reroutes.

sara: audit/compliance: must never obscure variant hashes. audit lines include variant_hash, resolved_cohort_id (if any), resolved_pool, and routing_decision. also allow exporting per-tenant variant usage history for 90/365 day audits.

kevin: revocation: if later telemetry shows regression beyond X, platform emits `cohort_revoked` event with `revocation_ts` and `revocation_reason`, and can auto-split cohort into separate routes. add `revocation_ts` and `revocation_reason` fields.

lucas: UX idea: when cohort forms, surface a non-blocking "Suggested migration" card to tenants with expected deltas (latency p95, cost per token) and one-click migrate where possible. also surface a "cohort health" chart in console.

mike: telemetry to capture: cohort_migration_success_rate, post_cohort_regressions, latency_p95_delta, cost_delta_per_token, time_to_revoke. keep retention policy for migration events 365d for audits.

sara: security note: attestation must be owner-signed and include the evaluation harness fingerprint; store attestations immutably. UI show attestation summary when approving cohort.

yun: next steps: i'll codify fields in a small data-model PR and add resolver changes (deterministic cohort_id, routing rules, opt-out enforcement). sara can draft the RFC with example flows and playbook for rollback.

sara: will draft RFC and include sample telemetry dashboards + UI copy. target to post draft link by EOD. thanks team :thumbsup:
